page: Amazon Web Services r5.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8175M processors. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and memory throughput. The server achieves a strong multi-core CPU performance score of 81870.14 in stress-ng and a PassMark CPU score of 57080.9. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4545.56 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 96.13 GB/sec. Database operations are a notable strength, evidenced by a PassMark database score of 21974.43 and Redis SET operations reaching 74.16 million operations per second.

Despite strong multi-core and database performance, the server exhibits limitations in specific workloads. Single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1207.0. Large language model text generation is a significant bottleneck due to the lack of GPU acceleration, resulting in a poor text generation speed of 5.25 tokens per second on medium models. Consequently, the r5.metal is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database operations, and enterprise software compilation, while being poorly suited for real-time LLM text generation or workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r5.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server designed for resource-intensive enterprise workloads. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8175M processor offering 96 vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The server lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, but features a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and excellent database execution speeds, with Redis SET operations reaching 74.16 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, and the absence of GPU acceleration leads to poor text generation speeds in large language model inference. This hardware profile makes the r5.metal highly cost-efficient for memory-heavy applications, large databases, and parallel software compilation, whereas it is less suitable for GPU-dependent machine learning or workloads requiring local NVMe storage.
